# Incident Report: Malware Infection on DESKTOP-GXMYNO2

**Capture:** 2022-01-07-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap (5,880 packets, single LAN interface, subnet 192.168.1.0/24, DC at 192.168.1.2)

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 192.168.1.216 | conv/DHCP/ARP |
| MAC | 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9 | ARP reply for 192.168.1.216 (frame set); DHCP request source MAC; matches eth.src on all traffic from .216 |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 | DHCP option 12 (frame ~1, `dhcp.option.hostname`); confirmed via DNS self-registration queries |
| Logged-in user | steve.smith | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ from 192.168.1.216 to DC 192.168.1.2 |
| Domain | spoonwatch.net (AD domain, DC = SPOONWATCH-DC, 192.168.1.2) | DNS SRV/LDAP queries, Kerberos traffic |

## Malware Family
**Vidar Stealer** — attribution is **behavioral** (no IDS/Suricata alert file was provided in the evidence directory; only the pcap and prior tshark-exported objects were present).

Behavioral basis:
- Client (192.168.1.216) makes a series of plain-HTTP POST/GET exchanges to a single bare IP, `2.56.57.108:80`, with no DNS lookup and no domain in the Host header — consistent with a hardcoded C2 IP.
- Seven files are fetched over this session with `.jpg` URIs (`/osk//1.jpg` through `/osk//7.jpg`, `Content-Type: image/jpeg` in the response) but each is actually a **Windows PE32 DLL**, confirmed via `file` magic-byte inspection of the tshark-exported objects. The DLL set (VCRUNTIME140.dll, MSVCP140.dll, CRYPT32/ADVAPI32 dependents, api-ms-win-crt-convert-l1-1-0.dll, etc.) matches the standard Vidar dependency bundle used to read/decrypt browser credential stores (NSS/SQLite-style libraries).
- A GET to `/osk//main.php` follows (empty 200 response — typical Vidar check-in/config beacon).
- The session ends with a large multipart POST to `/osk/` (379,629 bytes) whose body — recovered as the exported object `osk` — is a ZIP archive named **`_586169120.zip`**, containing paths such as `autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt` and `autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`. This is the classic Vidar stolen-data exfiltration archive layout (browser autofill/passwords/cookies staged into a zip and uploaded to the C2 over HTTP POST).

No delivery/infection-vector traffic (initial dropper, malspam, exploit page) is present in this capture — the capture begins with DHCP renewal and the malware is already resident; only the C2 check-in and post-infection exfiltration phases were captured.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `2.56.57.108:80` — sole non-Microsoft TCP destination in the capture; hosted the `/osk/` panel path used for DLL staging and data exfiltration (frames 1498–4830)

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg` through `/osk//7.jpg` (staged DLLs disguised as images)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php` (check-in/beacon)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` (exfiltration POST endpoint)

**Domain**
- None observed — malware communicated directly to the bare IP `2.56.57.108` with no DNS resolution or HTTP Host header, so no C2 domain can be grounded in this traffic.

**Files transferred (staged payload DLLs, downloaded from C2, disguised as .jpg)**
| Filename as served | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| 1.jpg | 16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660 |
| 2.jpg | a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba |
| 3.jpg | 3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd |
| 4.jpg | 334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4 |
| 5.jpg | e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78 |
| 6.jpg | 43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083 |
| 7.jpg | c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d |

**Exfiltrated artifact (uploaded from victim to C2)**
- Filename: `_586169120.zip` (multipart form field `filename=`, upload to `/osk/`), SHA256: `1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f`
- Contents include stolen browser autofill data (`autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`)

## Benign Context (not IOCs)
- Windows Update / Delivery Optimization traffic to `download.windowsupdate.com`, `au.download.windowsupdate.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com` (23.38.189.225/201, 8.253.189.126) — legitimate `.cab`/`am_delta_patch*.exe` (Microsoft Defender definition update) downloads
- Microsoft telemetry/services SNI: `v10/v20.events.data.microsoft.com`, `settings-win.data.microsoft.com`, `self.events.data.microsoft.com`, `client.wns.windows.com`, `www.bing.com`, `api.msn.com`, `fe2cr.update.microsoft.com`, `fe3cr.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`, `geo/cp801/kv801.prod.do.dsp.mp.microsoft.com`, `pti.store.microsoft.com`
- Active Directory/domain traffic: Kerberos, LDAP/CLDAP, DRSUAPI, SAMR, NBNS/SMB to DC 192.168.1.2 (SPOONWATCH-DC)
- SSDP/M-SEARCH multicast, LLMNR, mDNS — local network discovery noise

## Incident Summary
The Windows workstation DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 (192.168.1.216, MAC 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9), logged in as domain user `steve.smith` on the `spoonwatch.net` AD domain, was infected with malware behaviorally consistent with **Vidar Stealer**. The malware beaconed to a hardcoded C2 at `2.56.57.108:80`, downloaded seven support DLLs disguised as `.jpg` images under `/osk/`, checked in via `/osk//main.php`, and exfiltrated a 379 KB ZIP archive of stolen browser autofill data (`_586169120.zip`) via HTTP POST to `/osk/`. No initial infection vector is present in this capture; only the C2/exfiltration phase was recorded.
